statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress rises within the high band on a 5.18% 10-year yield at its highest since 2007, WTI at $92.41 and Brent at $104.32 with the Strait of Hormuz still disrupted, and a rejected Iranian reopening proposal that reporting now pairs with a privately expected resumption of strikes after the November midterms.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this publication.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a rejected Hormuz plan, a reported post-midterm strike expectation and a 5.18% 10-year yield hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. Contemporaneous reporting has the S&P 500 up 0.51% at 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.5% at 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93% at 51,828.62. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

Stress rises one point to 68 on three independent inputs that all hardened over the weekend. Rates remain the structural pressure: H.15 puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 2-year at 4.87%, with the 10-year at its highest level since 2007 after touching 5.22% on Thursday, and the 30-year mortgage rate at 7.45% is the highest in more than two years. Energy is the second: WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33%, and Brent at $104.32, down 2.14%, specifically on optimism that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen. That premise is now firmly withdrawn. Washington publicly rejected the Iranian seven-day proposal on Saturday, Tehran states it is still awaiting a definitive reply through mediators, and Wall Street Journal reporting carried by several outlets says the administration privately expects to resume strikes after the November midterms while remaining reluctant near term partly to preserve munitions. The third is a widening regional escalation: the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh, Riyadh schools shifted to remote learning on Sunday, and Houthi authorities attributed a Taiz market strike that killed seven to Saudi aircraft.

The important distinction is that none of this is yet a price path. Under this contract event importance, diplomatic reversal and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence until observed market structure supports Tail, so the mapped state stays EA_ON and the protection is expressed as a narrow danger window across the 22:00Z restart rather than a broad shutdown. The reported post-midterm framing also argues against an immediate discontinuity even as it keeps the waterway closed for longer. Cross-asset internals still argue against alignment: on the latest session 6 of 8 megacaps rose but dispersion was 1.92%, with MSFT up 3.66% against META down 3.33%, and 6 of 7 semiconductors rose with QCOM up 3.97% against INTC down 3.45%. That is rotation, not the uniform one-way alignment that would amplify Tail. A separate slow-burn input is AI-linked credit, where a reported Oracle force-majeure notice tied to a New Mexico data-centre project landed against a 10-year yield up roughly one percentage point year to date.

Confidence improves to 77. Verified index, volatility, yield, crude and calendar evidence is complete, the Brent level that could not be published last cycle is now corroborated by two independent sources at $104.32, and the weekend diplomatic and regional developments were each verified against multiple outlets. Offsetting that, there is still no live price path during the futures halt, and the shared Finviz context was 127 minutes old at this assessment with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so its breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were used only as labelled latest-session, non-real-time confirmation evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 band, Stress rose from 50 to 67, and Confidence decayed from 83 to a 67 trough around 08:00Z before recovering to 75 as weekend evidence was verified. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts from roughly 18:00Z into the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the rejected Hormuz proposal and the weekend Saudi-Houthi exchange meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Conditional Tail peaks at 17 in the first full hour after the restart, then decays through the Asian session as liquidity normalises, easing to single digits by the European open. A modest lift to 9 is carried across the 13:30Z US cash open and to 10 across the 14:30Z Dallas Fed manufacturing survey, where opening-auction continuation without a shallow pullback would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week. Every forecast hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.
